answer: Submitted hypothesis: At 1100 BCE, PC1 of the century-by-century capital PCA is a marked positive outlier relative to every later Younger Bronze Age slice. Thereafter PC1 steps down sharply from 1100 → 1000 BCE and continues to drift downward through 500 BCE. Full hypothesis text and supporting tables are in this handoff; artifacts at analysis/pca_yba.py (executed) and analysis/pca_yba_results.json.

payload.hypothesis: The PCA on the forms of capital in hundred-year time slices during the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE) shows that PC1 at the beginning of the period, 1100 BCE, is a marked positive outlier relative to every subsequent YBA slice and the y-axis can be interpreted as a general 'accumulated/intensive capital' axis (positive loadings on Hatchets/Swords, Daggers, House Size, Copper+Gold, Monument Count, Depot and Monument Size; ZSichel and ZKeform are constant in YBA and were dropped). PC1(1100 BCE) = +5.35 (YBA-only PCA, 62.5% variance) vs. PC1 mean over 1000-500 BCE = -0.89, a difference of +6.24 units or about +6.9 SD; the 1100 BCE value is +5.38 above the next-highest YBA score (1000 BCE = -0.03). A robustness PCA on all 39 slices (4300-500 BCE, PC1 = 30.3% variance) confirms the same pattern in scale: PC1(YBA subset) falls from 4.45 at 1100 BCE to 2.15 at 1000 BCE and to 0.78 by 500 BCE. Therefore 1100 BCE is a peak (terminal for the prior OBA-era configuration), followed by a single-century step-down to 1000 BCE and then a continued gradual decline through 500 BCE; the opening YBA horizon differs from the rest of the YBA span by being substantially and statistically extremely higher on PC1, with the difference dominated by the 1100->1000 BCE break.
payload.workflow: Loaded data/capital.csv (European-decimal commas inside quoted fields) with pandas; parsed numbers; filtered to YBA rows (BCE 500..1100, 7 slices); dropped zero-within-YBA-variance features (ZSichel, ZKeform); standardised features (z-score within the analysis window); ran PCA via SVD on the centred/scaled matrix (scipy.linalg.svd); oriented PC1 sign so that higher PC1 = higher capital; recorded loadings and per-slice scores; compared PC1 at 1100 BCE with the 1000-500 BCE subset (mean, min, max, std, excess, z-score). Repeated the full pipeline as a robustness check using all 39 rows from capital.csv (4300-500 BCE) and showed the YBA subset of that PCA. Persisted outputs to analysis/pca_yba_results.json. The full script is at analysis/pca_yba.py.
